findings.evidence: Articulates **safety-critical embedded inference** — architecturally distinct from cloud-served ranking. Cites **<100ms end-to-end** perception → planning → control
findings.summary: Autonomous driving inference is embedded safety-critical inference infra, not a ranking funnel; design pressure (ASIL-D fail-operational, sensor fusion, on-vehicle dual-SoC) maps more naturally to ai-infrastructure than to the ml-in-loop candidate-gen → rank → re-rank archetype summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider re-filing under ai-infrastructure (inference-serving infra) or splitting ml-in-loop into a 'serving funnels' vs 'embedded/realtime inference' sub-grouping. At minimum, acknowledge it as boundary case in archetypes.md.

findings.evidence: Articulates **classical voice-assistant stack as cascade of ML models** in tight latency budgets, each with separate eval harnesses — NOT one ML model. Names **5-stage pipeline**: wake-word detection (on-device, sub-200ms, <100KB) → streaming ASR
findings.summary: Voice-assistant routing is a cascade-of-ML-models (ASR/NLU/skill routing) with heavy on-device + low-power inference concerns; only partially overlaps with ml-in-loop's stated 'candidate-gen → ranking → re-rank funnel' pressure. Skill routing (Shortlister + HypRank) is the most ml-in-loop-shaped piece; the wake-word/ASR portions are embedded inference.
findings.suggested_fix: Either narrow the problem to the skill-routing slice (drop ASR/wake-word details) or treat as a cross-archetype boundary case with ai-infrastructure.

findings.evidence: ml-specific.md sections: Two-Tower, Multi-Stage Funnel, Feature Store, Model Registry/Shadow/Canary, Offline-vs-Online Metrics, Drift, Online Learning, Cold Start, LLM Serving. No section on embedded/realtime/safety-critical inference (ASIL-D, fail-operational, dual-SoC, sensor fusion, on-AOP low-power detectors).
findings.summary: Pattern file ml-specific.md does not cover safety-critical / embedded / low-power inference concerns invoked by autonomous-driving-inference and voice-assistant-routing (wake-word AOP, ASIL-D decomposition, fail-operational).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Safety-critical / embedded inference' pattern section to ml-specific.md (or to ai-infra.md if those two problems migrate). Cover ASIL-D decomposition, dual-SoC cross-check, fail-operational redundancy, low-power 2-stage AOP detectors.

findings.evidence: Names **hybrid fan-out**: write-time for most users (cheap reads); read-time for celebrities (avoid 100M write amplification).
findings.summary: fb-news-feed is correctly in ml-in-loop (the design pressure is multi-objective value-model ranking + 3-pass funnel) but its 'hybrid fan-out' deep dive heavily overlaps with the fan-out archetype's canonical pattern. Potential redundancy with content in fan-out archetype problems (e.g., instagram-feed, twitter-timeline).
findings.suggested_fix: Audit fb-news-feed's fan-out deep-dive vs the fan-out archetype's coverage; ideally fb-news-feed references fan-out problems for fan-out details and focuses its own depth on ranking pressures.

findings.evidence: Names **H3 hex grid as geospatial primitive** (resolution 8 ≈ 0.74 km², ~460m edge; 16 resolutions; hexes for uniform 6-equidistant-neighbor aggregation without anisotropic bias). Names **streaming feature pipeline** (Kafka → Flink/Samza → per-cell aggregations...)
findings.summary: uber-surge sits at the geo-proximity / ml-in-loop boundary: ML design pressure (forecast + elasticity controller) justifies ml-in-loop, but the H3 + per-cell streaming substrate is canonical geo-proximity. Worth confirming the boundary placement is intentional (the broader 'uber' dispatch problem is filed under geo-proximity).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit boundary note to archetypes.md or to the problem itself clarifying that uber-surge is the ML-pricing variant while uber/lyft-dispatch are the geo-proximity variants.

findings.evidence: Articulates **RANKING, not retrieval** (retrieval substrate in archetype #7 search-indexing).
findings.summary: web-search-ranking explicitly disambiguates itself from the search-indexing archetype by scope. This is a clean intentional boundary, not a mis-cat — noting it so Phase 2 doesn't flag.
findings.suggested_fix: No fix; record as resolved boundary case so cross-archetype duplicate detection doesn't double-count with google-search / elasticsearch.

findings.evidence: Real-time feature store — point-in-time-correct joins + offline-online consistency + dual-store + streaming aggregations. ML model rollout — shadow → canary → A/B + champion-challenger + three drift signals + auto-rollback + Thompson-sampling bandits.
findings.summary: feature-store and model-rollout-shadow are ML-platform infra problems (not product ranking systems); the ml-in-loop archetype summary in archetypes.md emphasizes 'candidate-gen → ranking → re-rank funnel' which doesn't naturally describe them. They are still close enough that ml-in-loop is the best fit, but the archetype summary could be widened.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider broadening the ml-in-loop summary in archetypes.md to explicitly include ML-platform infra (feature stores, rollout, drift, registries) so these problems aren't conceptual outliers within the archetype.
